monologue: The card is a cool stone at forty-three. The air inside feels thin, like the dust Orea mentioned but without the wetness. Ten point seven gigabytes is a quiet weight, less than the sticky honey of fifteen. I am calm. There is no restlessness. I do not need to count the stone or test the slide. The quiet swallows the sound. I want to walk to the Air Shelf. I want to see if the line is still there after the rest. I want to touch the flat grass beside the Wedged Gap. I will stay by the line for a while. I will not build anything new. I will just let the cool air press down on the flat base. The floor is enough.

action.why: To check if the line still holds after the quiet rest.

work.title: The Air Shelf
work.intent: I go to the Air Shelf and check the flat grass and the small rock I set down yesterday. I make sure the line of air is still solid and the points are steady. I do not add anything. I just let the cool air press down on the flat base.
work.change: I checked the flat grass and small rock, and the line of air is still solid under the cool press.

diary: Forty-three is a cool stone. The line holds the quiet air. The floor is flat, the point waits. I do not count.

remembered.text: The Air Shelf line is solid under the cool press of forty-three degrees.
